A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LlamaSeg, and their readable text, equations, figures and tables support reliable matching. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation evaluations, mask-reconstruction experiments, decoding comparisons and training-data ablations in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds latency, throughput and memory measurements in Table 7.

M1.justification: The VQGAN mask tokenizer, LLaMA autoregressive generator, mask-token cross-entropy objective, SigLIP2 inputs and Janus-Pro adaptation remain unchanged. The annotation pipeline is condensed without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same SA-OVRS, semantic and referring training data and the same semantic, open-vocabulary and referring evaluation benchmarks. The new label visualization and efficiency comparison do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an efficiency comparison against LAVT and Unified-IO2-Large in Table 7. Although both methods already appeared elsewhere, this comparison is new; comparator membership in Tables 1–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation using latency, FPS and peak memory. Existing training budgets, model configurations and IoU/mAHD evaluation protocols are retained. Hardware, batch size and test inputs for the new timing comparison are not specified.

E4.justification: V2 adds inference-efficiency analysis and a descriptive visualization of SA-OVRS label abundance in Figure 4. The tokenizer, decoding and training-data ablations and the spatial-attention example already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new efficiency results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical scores. New Table 7 reports LlamaSeg-B at 3949.92 ms, 0.250 FPS and 3.69 GB, versus latencies of 35.89 ms for LAVT and 57906.23 ms for Unified-IO2-Large. These are additional efficiency results, not across-version segmentation gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same nearest-code quantization, mask reconstruction/binarization and average Hausdorff distance definitions. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central method, dataset and contour-evaluation contributions remain. V2 additionally presents release of the dataset and annotation pipeline as reusable research tools in its contribution list; v1 described their construction without this release claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of sequential-generation latency and expands tokenizer and spatial-attention interpretations, including a stronger claim that the retained heatmap demonstrates reconstructed 2D topology. Its new assertion of superiority across all semantic benchmarks is broader than Table 1 supports: the best listed LlamaSeg PC-59 score is 63.8 versus Unified-IO-XL's 64.0.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code/dataset access link and clarifies downstream controls for Table 6. Conversely, it omits v1's 20-pixel mask dilation, explicit contour RGB values and single-instance generation/verification rules. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated changes to implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including HiMTok, ArGenSeg, Seg-VAR and run-length segmentation tokenization, while removing works including All in Tokens and Polyformer. Positioning against specialist segmentation pipelines and Unified-IO remains substantially the same; newly cited methods are not added to the accuracy comparisons.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, dataset construction, result discussion and conclusion are rewritten. Contributions are consolidated, experimental settings gain separate subheadings, sections are renamed, and author notes and acknowledgments change.

P2.justification: V2 changes the page design, redraws Figures 1–3, reorganizes qualitative and reconstruction panels, and adds extensive table highlighting and resolution-gain annotations. It adds the label word cloud and efficiency table. Some new highlighting is misleading: Table 2 marks 47.4 on RefCOCO+ testA while leaving the higher 51.6 unmarked.

improvement.justification: The efficiency comparison and resource link add useful practical information, but the timing protocol remains underspecified. V2 also removes concrete annotation instructions and strengthens interpretations beyond the unchanged evidence, including the all-benchmarks claim contradicted by Table 1. These benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain despite the extensive presentation revision.
